rv.q: Happily, Callum Francis, who has played the part in Britain, Australia and, briefly, on Broadway, meets them.
Lauper and Fierstein are never onstage, but their spirits elevate a very conventional show with wit and sweetness.

Who doesn't love Cyndi Lauper? A proudly idiosyncratic pop priestess since the early '80s, she's always been way more real than her contemporary, Madonna, let alone such 21st century descendants as Lady Gaga and Nicki Minaj. Rocking the thrift-store ...
So for whatever minor faults the production might have, it scarcely matters when it sends you out into the night in a haze of rainbow glitter and good vibes.
Rest assured, Kinky Boots is a fantastically feel-good time.
Still, boasting a powerhouse performance from Billy Porter as Lola, the drag queen who’s also a trained boxer, the damn thing works.
But Kinky Boots still has its big, glittery heart intact.
The quality of this off-Broadway revival is no less high than what you would have seen at the Theatre on opening night.
What the duo has conjured together in 'Kinky Boots' is a vibrant, if choppy tale with bold, brassy music that delivers on its promise, and a story that is often predictable.
My second look didn’t bowl me over; I still don’t think it’s kinky enough.
It has plenty of surface glamour, but its best qualities are an abundance of heart and soul.
If audiences are willing to skip over the wide schism that permeates the plot, Kinky Boots retains the feel-good sentiment.
